transcript.text: Beko vented dryer, drum goes round fine but it's just blowing cold air. Had it about 6 years. What part do I need?

If the drum turns and the fan is blowing but the air stays cold, the most likely fault is in the heater circuit. On a 6-year-old Beko vented dryer, the usual suspects are:

1. Heating element – most common.
2. Thermal cut-out / thermal fuse / thermostat mounted on the heater housing – often fails because of restricted airflow or lint build-up.
3. Less commonly, damaged wiring, timer/control-board heater relay, or door-switch circuitry.

You cannot reliably order the exact part without the dryer’s model number (usually on a label just inside the door opening, on the rear panel, or around the door frame). Search using the full model number plus terms such as:

• “heater element”
• “heater assembly”
• “thermal cutout kit”
• “thermostat kit”

For many Beko vented dryers it is sensible to replace the heater element assembly with its thermostats/cut-outs, rather than fitting only an element—provided testing confirms the heater circuit is open.

Before buying parts:

• Unplug it from the mains.
• Clean the lint filter, vent hose and outside vent thoroughly. A blocked vent can overheat the dryer and blow a thermal cut-out.
• Remove the rear panel and check the heater element and thermostats with a multimeter for continuity. An open-circuit element or cut-out identifies the failed part.
• Check for burnt connectors around the heater, as loose terminals can also stop heating.

Do not bypass a thermal fuse/cut-out: it is a fire-safety device.

If you send the full Beko model number from the rating label, I can narrow down the correct heater/cut-out part or assembly.

It says DV7110 on the front but I can't get to the rear label, it's wedged in a tight alcove. I don't have a multimeter either. The vent hose was absolutely rammed with fluff before it stopped heating. Can you tell me which part it most likely is from that?

Given the vent hose was badly blocked, the most likely failed part is the heater thermal cut-out / thermal fuse, rather than the drum motor or controls.

A blocked vent makes the heater overheat. The safety cut-out then opens the heater circuit, so the dryer still tumbles and blows air but it is cold. Depending on the exact DV7110 version, Beko may supply this as:

• a thermal cut-out / thermostat kit, fitted to the heater housing, or
• a complete heater element assembly with thermostats/cut-outs.

The heating element itself may still be OK, but without a meter there is no safe way to distinguish a blown thermal cut-out from a failed element. Since the vent was “rammed with fluff”, I’d put the cut-out first on the list.

Important points:

• Do not use it until the vent hose, wall vent and lint filter path are fully cleaned.
• Do not bypass the thermal cut-out; it is a fire-safety part.
• “DV7110” alone may not be enough to order accurately—there are often suffixes/production variants, and heater parts can differ.
• If paying someone to repair it, tell them: “Drum and fan run, but no heat, after a severely blocked vent hose. Please test the heater element and thermal cut-out.” That should direct them straight to the likely area.

If you have to choose a part without testing, buy the correct heater assembly including its thermostats/cut-outs for the full model/serial version, rather than only an element. But ideally get the model label or have the heater circuit checked first, because ordering the wrong Beko heater assembly is easy.
